_what: ML-KEM-768 cases extracted from NIST ACVP, vendored so the vector generator needs no KEM implementation. ALL TEN of NIST's ML-KEM-768 decapsulation cases are here rather than a sample, so there is no selection to justify -- without them the oracle would cover keyGen and encapsulation only, while `V2-11` and `V2-13` are emitted THROUGH decapsulation, so a KEM with a subtly wrong decapsulation path would pass the advertised acceptance test and the conformance suite could certify wrong scanner behaviour. FIVE OF THE TEN ARE `modified ciphertext`, which is IMPLICIT REJECTION with NIST's own expected secret -- an external witness for the single property this whole ladder is shaped around.
_rule: Tier 1 is ACVP and we generate nothing. These are INPUTS to the tier-2 generator, never outputs of it.
_hex_case: Lowercase throughout, normalised on vendoring. ACVP publishes uppercase; a conformance runner comparing a tier-1 value against a tier-2 one as strings would fail on case alone, and the tier-2 generator emits lowercase. The bytes are unchanged and the upstream sha256 recorded above is of the ORIGINAL file.
_decapsulation_note: `dk` here is the EXPANDED 2 400-byte decapsulation key, which is ACVP's representation and NOT the one this specification uses: §1 requires the 64-byte (d, z) seed, and the difference is what makes a delegated tracking key 64 bytes instead of 2 400. So the acceptance check consumes these through an expanded-key entry point that exists for this purpose only -- see `vecprim.kem_decaps_expanded`. Our own derivations never take this path.
